title: Day 1 · Meet Python
summary: What Python is and how programs run
content:
Python is a readable programming language used for websites, automation, data science, and AI. A program is a set of instructions the computer follows.

Try reading this line:
print("Hello, world!")

The print function displays a value on the screen.
question: What does print("Hello") do?

title: Day 2 · Variables
content:
A variable stores a value under a name. Python figures out the value's type for you.

name = "Maya"
age = 20

Use print(name) to display the value.
question: Which line stores 20 in age?

title: Day 3 · Numbers & math
content:
Python supports integers and decimal numbers. You can add, subtract, multiply, and divide with +, -, *, and /.

score = 8 + 2
print(score)  # 10
question: What is 7 * 3 in Python?

title: Day 4 · Text strings
content:
Text values are called strings and are wrapped in quotes. Join strings with +, or use an f-string to insert a value.

name = "Sam"
print(f"Hi, {name}!")
question: Which is a string?

title: Day 5 · Get user input
content:
input() pauses the program and reads what someone types. Its result is text, even when the user types a number.

name = input("Your name? ")
print(name)
question: What type of value does input() return?

title: Day 6 · Make decisions
question: Which keyword handles the other case?

title: Day 7 · Comparisons
content:
Comparisons produce True or False. Use == to check equality, != for not equal, and > or < for ordering.

5 > 3  # True
5 == 3 # False
question: Which operator checks whether two values are equal?

title: Day 8 · Lists
content:
A list holds an ordered collection. Items are separated by commas, and positions start at zero.

colors = ["red", "blue"]
print(colors[0])  # red
question: What is the first list index?

title: Day 9 · For loops
summary: Repeat an action for each item
question: How many times does the loop body run?
options: Only if the list is empty

title: Day 10 · While loops
summary: Repeat while a condition is true
content:
A while loop repeats as long as its condition stays true. Update values inside the loop so it can eventually stop.

count = 0
while count < 3:
    count += 1
question: When does a while loop stop?

title: Day 11 · Functions
content:
Define a function with def. Call it by writing its name followed by parentheses.

def greet():
    print("Hello!")

greet()
question: Which keyword defines a function?

title: Day 12 · Function inputs
content:
Parameters let a function receive information. Arguments are the values passed when you call it.

def greet(name):
    print(f"Hi, {name}")

greet("Ari")
question: In greet(name), what is name?

title: Day 13 · Return values
content:
return sends a result back to the code that called the function.

def double(number):
    return number * 2

result = double(4)
question: What does return do?

title: Day 14 · Dictionaries
question: How do you look up Lee's age?

title: Day 15 · Tuples & sets
question: Which collection keeps only unique values?

title: Day 16 · Useful string tools
content:
Strings have useful methods. strip() removes extra outer whitespace, and lower() makes letters lowercase.

answer = " YES ".strip().lower()
question: What does strip() remove?

title: Day 17 · List tools
content:
Lists can grow and shrink. append() adds to the end; len() tells you how many items are present.

items = ["pen"]
items.append("book")
question: What does append() do?
options: Adds an item to the end

title: Day 18 · Modules
content:
A module is a file of reusable Python code. Import one to use its functions.

import random
print(random.randint(1, 6))
question: Which keyword brings in a module?

title: Day 19 · Errors & debugging
content: An error message often points to the line that needs attention. Read it carefully, check spelling and indentation, then try again.
question: What is a good first debugging step?

title: Day 20 · Handle exceptions
question: Which block handles a matching error?

title: Day 21 · Read & write files
content:
Use open() with a context manager to work with files. The with block closes the file for you.

with open("notes.txt") as file:
    text = file.read()
question: Why use with open(...)?

title: Day 22 · Comprehensions
content:
A list comprehension builds a new list from an iterable.

squares = [n * n for n in range(4)]
# [0, 1, 4, 9]
question: What does range(4) produce?

title: Day 23 · Classes & objects
summary: Model things with your own types
content:
A class describes a kind of object. An object is one instance of that class.

class Pet:
    pass

my_pet = Pet()
question: What is my_pet here?

title: Day 24 · Object properties
question: What does self refer to?

title: Day 25 · Inheritance
question: What does Dog(Animal) suggest?

title: Day 26 · Boolean logic
content: and is true when both sides are true. or is true when either side is true. not flips a Boolean value.
question: When is A and B true?

title: Day 27 · APIs & JSON
content: APIs let programs exchange data. JSON is a common text format for that data. Python's json module can encode and decode it.
question: What is JSON commonly used for?

title: Day 28 · Virtual environments
content: A virtual environment gives a project its own place for installed packages, helping keep projects separate.
question: Why use a virtual environment?

title: Day 29 · Mini project
content: Make a tiny quiz program: keep questions in a list, ask for an answer, compare it, and keep score. Break the project into small functions.
question: What is a useful first step on a mini project?

title: Day 30 · Keep learning
summary: Celebrate and choose your next project
content: You made it through 30 days! Review the topics that felt tricky, then build something small: a number guessing game, a study tracker, or a simple data report.
question: What is a great next step?
